title: russias ryazan oil refinery has stopped operations after sept 6 drone attack 2026 09 10
text:
Sept 10 (Reuters) - Russia's Rosneft (ROSN.MM)
, opens new tab
-owned Ryazan oil refinery stopped operations following the September 6 drone attack, two industry sources told Reuters on Thursday.
Ukraine continues ​its strikes on Russian energy infrastructure in an effort ‌to undermine the country's economy as the war has raged for more than four and a half years.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said the attacks were ​meant to sow discord within Russia.
The sources said that the ​oil refinery's main unit, CDU-6, as well as another ⁠primary unit, CDU-4, were halted following the attack.
CDU-6, which caught fire ​in the attack, as the sources said, has the capability to ​process 8 million metric tons of oil per year, or around 160,000 barrels per day, accounting for almost a half of the plant's capacity.
CDU-4 can process 4 ​million tons of oil per year.
Another primary unit, CDU-3, has ​been under maintenance since mid-May.
The sources said the repair of the damaged units could ‌take ⁠up to several weeks.
Rosneft did not reply to a request for comment about the attack on the plant, located some 200 kilometres (124 miles) southeast of Moscow.
The Ryazan oil refinery, which feeds Moscow with fuel, ​was also attacked by ​drones on ⁠May 15. The sources said the repair works had continued until around mid-July since then.
It was struck by ​drones too on July 29 and has stopped operations ​for ⁠around two to three weeks, the sources said.
According to industry sources, the refinery processed 13.1 million tons of crude oil in 2024, accounting for ⁠about ​4.9% of Russia's total refining throughput.
It produced ​2.2 million tons of gasoline, 3.4 million tons of diesel fuel and 4.3 million ​tons of fuel oil that year.
